title: In-depth characterization of gastrointestinal tumors for personalized therapy
summary: The main objective of the study is to thoroughly characterize the tumor, abdominal fluid, blood, saliva, urine and stool of each individual patient (including examination of the altered genetic information and characteristics of the tumor cells, the immune response, and the cells surrounding the tumor [tumor microenvironment]) and to correlate them with clinical parameters such as the survival of each patient, recurrence or spread of the tumor, or the response to certain therapies. The rapid development of new technologies in recent years has revealed the individual diversity of tumors. Tumors that appear identical morphologically (shape, form and structure) differ considerably in their tumor biology. Standardized therapies are highly variable in their effectiveness. The integration of molecular analyses into clinical diagnostics could help to identify new drug target structures and characteristics that predict the effectiveness of a treatment in order to develop individualized multimodal therapy regimens for each individual patient in the future with the best possible prognosis and quality of life.
conditions: Histologically proven or suspected gastrointestinal tumor (e.g. esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, cholangiocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastrointestinal neuroendocrine neoplasia)

interventions.name: Patients with histologically proven or suspected gastrointestinal tumors scheduled for elective tumor resection/biopsy will be recruited for this trial.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Histologically proven or suspected gastrointestinal tumor (e.g. esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, cholangiocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastrointestinal neuroendocrine neoplasia) on cross-sectional imaging with planned surgical resection/biopsy
-	≥ 18 years of age
-	Capacity for consent and written informed consent
-	Patient considered to tolerate surgery
Exclusion criteria:
-	American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score > III
-	Inability to comply with study and/or follow-up procedures
-	(language) problems in understanding the patient information document explaining the present clinical trial
-	Any condition which could result in an undue risk for the patient in the opinion of the investigator
